page: Amazon Web Services r7a.16xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro System and fourth-generation AMD EPYC 9R14 processors. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 64 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading, running at a clock frequency of 3.7 GHz. Hardware vector acceleration is supported via AVX, AVX-512, and AVX512 VNNI instruction sets. It features 512 GB of high-speed 5 GHz DDR5 memory, yielding an allocation ratio of 8 GB per core, backed by 32 MB of L3 cache per core complex.

The hardware configuration omits local NVMe instance storage and discrete GPU accelerators, relying on remote EBS volumes for persistent block storage. Network connectivity is rated at a baseline throughput of 25 Gbps. The architecture delivers massive uncached large-block read memory bandwidth measuring 285.19 GB/sec alongside uncached write bandwidth of 155.75 GB/sec, while cached read operations reach 9,203.38 GB/sec.

Benchmark evaluations place the system in the top tier for multi-threaded processing and in-memory operations. It registered a multi-core Geekbench score of 22,293 and a PassMark CPU score of 92,120.1. In-memory data throughput is exceptionally high, executing 137.08 million Redis SET operations per second and maintaining 58.18 GB/sec in static web serving benchmarks. Large-scale compilation and ray tracing benchmarks similarly place in the top decile.

With its 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio and 64 non-hyperthreaded physical cores, the r7a.16xlarge offers high qualitative cost efficiency for resource-dense enterprise workloads requiring large in-memory footprints. The primary tradeoff is the total lack of onboard disk storage, necessitating external network storage configurations. The instance is well matched for large in-memory databases like Redis, enterprise SAP deployments, distributed data analytics engines, and heavy relational database management systems.
description: Amazon Web Services r7a.16xlarge is a memory-optimized instance driven by AMD EPYC 9R14 processors on the AWS Nitro System. Featuring the x86_64 architecture, it supplies 64 dedicated physical cores running at 3.7 GHz without multithreading, combined with 512 GB of DDR5 memory at an 8 GB per core ratio. The platform contains no local SSD storage or discrete GPUs, using network-attached volumes alongside a 25 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark results demonstrate top-tier execution across multi-core compute and memory-bound tasks, registering 137.08 million Redis SET operations per second and a Geekbench multi-core score of 22,293. The instance balances extensive DDR5 memory bandwidth against reliance on remote storage, delivering high efficiency for memory-intensive enterprise applications including in-memory caches, large relational databases, and real-time big data analytics engines.
